current.summary: One open living and dining room under the exposed roof: dark beams and rafters with a weathered boarded deck, sloping down over the dining end. Warm white plastered walls. Sitting area: grey sofa (2.1 m) facing a wall-mounted TV; under the TV a 1950s painted sideboard on hairpin legs, above it a timber shelf with trailing plants; a trunk covered with a tapestry serves as coffee table. Behind the sofa, the stepped white masonry: a daybed niche with dark cushions, and above it the high ledge with a row of recesses under the cut-off old beam stubs — each recess now has a white up/down wall light. An arched opening (black sheet for now) leads to the kitchen. Dining end: dark extendable table with four green velvet chairs, a tall dark-wood dresser (wine and display), and the two old olive-green built-in cupboards — one glazed (china), one panelled with a paint-strip test patch and a raw open recess above it used as a shelf. Between dining and back doors: the exposed brick panel with a wall light over the antique bar counter. Back doors (wood, glazed, with wooden shutters) sit in a recess and open onto a small balcony; front doors with internal shutters open onto the front terrace. Also: gilt mirror over a wrought-iron wine-rack console, brass and glass-drop chandelier, cage pendants. Floor: large light-grey tiles.

target.concept: DRAFT for discussion — let the roof lead. Warm lime-white walls with their soft texture so the dark beams, the weathered boards and the brick panel do the talking. GREEN IS ALREADY THE HOUSE'S THREAD — the old cupboards, the outside of the front doors, the kitchen units, the velvet chairs — so make it deliberate: restore the two built-in cupboards in one chosen historic green and pick that same family for the daybed bolsters. Build the niche into a proper daybed, make the high ledge a lit display shelf, put the lighting into one warm family (aged brass, linen) with uplights washing the boards, and warm the floor with a large earth-toned rug under the sofa.

target.renderPrompt: Photorealistic interior photograph, same camera angle, same room geometry, same windows, doors, beams and walls — do not move or invent architecture. Remove ALL clutter: boxes, tools, clothes, bags, bottles, cables, packaging. Restyle as a warm, calm Sicilian mountain-village living room. Keep the dark timber roof beams and weathered plank ceiling exactly as they are, keep the exposed brick panel, keep the antique wooden bar and the gilt mirror. Walls: soft hand-finished lime plaster in warm white (Farrow & Ball Lime White). The stepped white masonry niche becomes a built-in daybed with tailored oatmeal linen cushions and olive-green bolsters. The high ledge is a tidy display shelf with a few ceramics and books, softly uplit, washing warm light onto the plank ceiling. One family of aged-brass and linen light fittings. Large flat-weave rug in terracotta and earth tones on the light grey tile floor; the grey sofa dressed with linen cushions in oatmeal, terracotta and olive (no tropical prints). If the old built-in cupboards are visible, restore them in a muted historic olive green. Late-afternoon warm light, 2700K lamps on, editorial interior photography, no people.
